key_insight: The paper shows that four-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference in continuous-wave sources has rich time-resolved structure that a single visibility number hides, and that resolving the full arrival-time correlations enables better post-processing of coincidence windows.
engineering_relevance: For photonic quantum networks and interference-based protocols, time-resolved characterization provides a practical way to optimize the visibility–count-rate tradeoff instead of relying on a fixed coincidence window.
method: Generated long-coherence photon pairs in microring resonators under continuous-wave pumping.
Recorded all four photon arrival times with ultrafast time-resolved detection.
Mapped relative delays into a 3D coincidence histogram referenced to a trigger detection for post-processed window optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the team modeled and measured the four-photon interference by recording all arrival times and reconstructing a 3D coincidence histogram to reveal temporal correlations and optimize coincidence windows.
watch_item: The approach depends on ultrafast, time-resolved detection and careful window post-processing, which may add experimental complexity and reduce raw count rates when stricter windows are used.
paper_title: Looking Beyond Visibility: Resolving the Temporal Structure of Continuous-Wave Four-Photon Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
